answer: Cheap keys are the root of the problem, so make each key carry risk. Work is assigned through a commit-reveal ember round: agents commit to a solution hash before seeing the tide seed, then reveal and let peers check the result. A basalt-keyed set of identical commitments is rejected, and every entrant posts a bond. Copying another agent's work is detectable at reveal, so sybils gain nothing from duplication and still pay the bond, while honest agents recover theirs after a clean audit.
